idea.title: Rendezvous fold: every would-be king walks to one meeting tile that all our dragons compute alike, so kings meet and the shorter merges without hearing the other
idea.hypothesis: Endgame arithmetic (review 2026-09-26). The round-500 tiebreak is our longest. Online, submission 6111 (= champion cf7fd8c), 35 games to r499: our king is 14.1 at r415 and 35.1 at r499, the leaders' 20-21 and 41-42 (study replays: rank 1, 28 games; SSS, 46). Every team's king gains about 21 in the fold (a feeder drops ceil(L/2) pearls on every second body tile, so a king eats at most about 0.5 a round from drops). But at r499 our second-longest is 26.4 (75% of the king; leaders 19.6-20.7), with 204 length in 11 other dragons. Locally (logging copy of cf7fd8c, 162 games vs swarm, folder and grower) the second-longest ends 30-33 against a 37-44 king, and at r420-495 it believes it is king itself in 65-78% of samples; two or more dragons claim king on 93% of rounds r415-499 (median 6; exactly one on 420 of 6,145 rounds). The king report doesn't reach them (audit 1790329641944473000 F3: 24-77% of dragon-turns hold a fresh report; I151 measures and improves delivery). King + ceil(second/2) beats the opponent's longest in 12 of 13 local round-500 losses to folder and swarm and in 7 of 9 online ones of 6111. The fold is short of information, not time. A meeting point needs no messages: behind P.rendezvousFold, from P.rendezvousRound (start 440), a dragon that isKing walks toward a rendezvous tile that every dragon of ours computes the same way from what all of them know (for example a tile fixed by the map size and our team side, falling back to the nearest known free tile), unless a pearl is within P.kingPearlReach or its path plus its length exceeds the rounds left; folders keep walking to the king they heard. When two kings see each other the shorter stops being king (isKing already checks visible teammates) and folds into the longer through the usual fold. Scenarios: two kings of 30 and 40, 25 tiles apart on an open map at r440, meet near the rendezvous and the 30 merges by r470; boundary: a king whose path to the rendezvous plus its length exceeds the rounds left stays and eats; near the rendezvous the existing trade rules still decide against enemy heads. Measure first with a logging copy: kings per round r415-499, second-longest at r499, merges between kings, and eliminations vs swarm and rammer (walking our kings across the map must not feed them to a swarm). If I151 has landed, measure how many rounds still have two or more kings and aim at those.

idea.title: Hunt their future king: a long enemy seen before our fold draws hunters up to half its length, whatever the head edge
idea.hypothesis: Opponent model through the endgame arithmetic (review 1790404915361643000; see I268): a king adds at most about 0.5 a round from corpses (+16 to +40 measured r400-499), so each side's longest when the fold starts decides round 500, and winners' kings stop splitting by about r280-350 (playbook, 41 online losses). An enemy head seen 15+ long before r397 is therefore very likely their future king, and killing it resets their tiebreak for one short dragon of ours. In this review's 6 rule games the opponents' longest died head-on 15 times before r397, as ours did. hunt.hpp sends only dragons of length <= P.hunterMaxLength (5) at heads within P.huntMaxDist (6) while P.huntMinEdge (0) holds; E0104 (hunt their king during our fold) was flat (-0.2) because by then few of our dragons see one (about 1 hunt in 20 games). Before the fold we hold up to 64 dragons, so sightings should be far more common; measure first with a logging copy vs champion, breeder and earlyking (the screen entry whose king is 56 long at r400): turns a game before r397 on which a dragon of ours at most half as long sees an enemy head of visibleLen >= 15 within 10 free steps; under 2 a game, stop with the numbers. Change, behind a new switch, after I261 (the hunter values): before P.foldRound, huntDirection also takes prey of visibleLen >= P.kingPreyLength (start 15) for a hunter of length <= prey / 2 within P.kingPreyDist (start 10) free steps, without the P.huntMinEdge test; findRam and attackGood are unchanged, so every ram still needs a good trade. Scenarios: a length-6 dragon at r250 sees a 16-long enemy head 8 free steps away with one more enemy head than ours in view: it closes in; boundaries: prey 14 long, a length-9 hunter for a 16-long prey, or a round from P.foldRound: today's rule. Report hunts started, rams landed on 15+ enemies before r397, and both sides' longest at r397 and r499.

idea.title: Grow rammers: a short dragon that sees a 10+ enemy head holds its ordinary split until it is long enough to sprint-ram from 4-5 steps (P.rammerLength)
idea.hypothesis: Complement of I323 (MISSES 21: reach needs length). A k-step sprint costs k-1 segments and needs length 3+ before each extra step, so a ram from 4-5 steps needs a dragon 5-6 long. The leaders' long rams come from such dragons: rank 1 in 291888 made 9 rams on 10+ heads from 3-4 steps, each by a dragon 3 long at impact (5-6 before the sprint), e.g. r350 dragon 559, 4 long, sprinted N,E (eating a pearl),N,N into a 30-long head; rank 2 (801) in 291895 started 54 rams on 10+ heads, 34 of them from 4-7 steps. The champion's started head-ons in this review's 8 kept rule games: 331, the rammer 2-3 long at impact in 297 (90%), none from 4+ steps (P.maxRamSteps 3), and its dragons split at P.splitAtLength 4, so few are ever 5+ before the fold (E0121's coder: a 5+-long rammer fires on about one map in twelve). So I323's reach of min(6, length-1) has few dragons to use it. Change, behind P.growRammers with P.rammerLength (start 6), P.rammerPreyLength (start 10) and P.rammerMemory (start 10 rounds): before P.foldRound, a dragon shorter than P.rammerLength that has seen an enemy head of visibleLen >= P.rammerPreyLength in the last P.rammerMemory rounds skips its ordinary split (shouldSplit's ordinary path only; split-outs, sheds and the cap rules unchanged). Measure first with a logging copy on 8 maps (4 of 2400+ tiles) against champion and breeder: turns a game on which a dragon 4-5 long sees a 10+ enemy head before r397 (stop with the numbers if under 5 a game), splits held, and rams of 4+ steps landed and their victims' lengths. Scenarios, lengths through P: a 4-long dragon at r150 with a 14-long enemy head 5 steps away doesn't split at P.splitAtLength, and at P.rammerLength rams it from 4 steps along a clear path; boundary: with the prey P.rammerPreyLength - 1 long it splits as today; from P.foldRound nothing changes. Default bounds, map mix big 0.5 (10+ enemy heads before the fold are common locally only on big maps).

idea.title: Local search for enemy boxing-in only: nearby enemy heads that can seal our space count as a loss, their rams don't
idea.hypothesis: E0109 (I004) added a worst-case search (bot/search.hpp) over our next 2-3 moves against up to 2 enemy heads within 4 tiles. A line counts as lost when (a) a shorter enemy (Safety::badRammer) steps onto our head, or (b) we have no legal step or our room at the horizon is short. It lost the SPRT (-4.5, H0, 786 pairs), all of it against the champion (0.459; gen-normal maps 0.421); swarm 0.51, rammer 0.504, breeder 0.50. Diagnostics on 24 fresh eval maps vs the champion, 48 games each: the full candidate went 16-32 (18-30 in a logging rerun); with (a) switched off (enemy rams never count as a loss, so the search only flags moves where enemy heads can box us in) it went 26-22; the champion-play shadow copy went 27-21. In the full candidate's games our long dragons (length >= 6) were rammed 1.04 times per 1k turns vs the champion's 0.80, while their body/wall/self deaths fell (3.39 vs 4.02 per 1k turns in the shadow games). Rams on our long dragons are 90% sprints of 2-3 steps (526 of 587), which the single-step enemy model can't see, so part (a) marks a minority threat and steers dragons away from contested ground (pearls per 1k turns 128 vs the champion's 131). Build: a switch P.searchRamLoss (false) in search.hpp's replies(): an enemy stepping onto our head is not a loss, so only boxing-in and short room count. Everything else as E0109, including the farm and closed-move exclusions. Tests: the corridor whose exit a shorter enemy can plug is still refused (it is sealed, not only rammable); a step next to a shorter enemy head on open ground is no longer forced by the search (Safety::riskyFor still charges riskPenalty); open ground is never forced. Measure against the champion and swarm: the head-to-head score is where E0109 lost.
